# Araññajātaka (Ja 348)

**ID:** Ja 348
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-1
**Title (Pali):** Araññajātaka
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** From the Wilderness
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/ja348
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul3.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Araññajātaka* (Ja 348) is a birth story set at Jetavana, delivered by the Buddha concerning the seduction of a youth by a coarse girl, a narrative whose full backstory is cross-referenced to the *Cullanāradakassapajātaka* [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1883]. In the past story, the Bodhisatta lived as an ascetic in the forest with his son after the death of his wife [Fausböll 1883]. While the father is away gathering fruits, a young woman tempts the son and entices him to break his moral practice and leave with her; when the father returns, the young ascetic recites an opening verse inquiring about the moral character and practices of people one should associate with upon leaving the forest for the village (*Araññā gāmam āgamma kimsīlam kimvatam aham...*) [Fausböll 1883]. In response, the Bodhisatta delivers three admonitory verses, guiding his son back to the ascetic life; both subsequently cultivate the *kasiṇa* meditations, preserve their absorption (*jhāna*), and gain rebirth in the Brahma realm [Fausböll 1883]. In modern scholarship, the Jātaka is noted for its canonical depiction of ordinary human consciousness as fickle and restless like "a monkey's mind" (*kapicitta*) [Revire 2016].

Regarding parallels and textual reuse, SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus both confirm that the verses of the *Araññajātaka* correspond closely to the *Haliddirāgajātaka* (Ja 435), where §1.1–4.4 of Ja 348 aligns with Ja 435 §2.1–6.4 [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records six matches with the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (totaling over 1,000 shared characters), while detecting no cross-language matches scoring 10 or above [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, SuttaCentral lists thematic and verse-level parallels with Dhammapada 391 (along with its parallels in the Gāndhārī Dharmapada, Patna Dharmapada, Udānavarga, and Chinese versions T 210, T 212, and T 213) and Itivuttaka 97 (*Kalyāṇasīla Sutta*, cf. T 765.122) [SuttaCentral].
